praetzellis.source: Treasure Island (version 2), ch. 3, read by Adrian Praetzellis, LibriVox, 26.5-62.7 s. Recording public domain (LibriVox); text by R. L. Stevenson (d. 1894), public domain worldwide
praetzellis.text: About noon I stopped at the captain's door with some cooling drinks and medicines. He was lying very much as we had left him, only a little higher, and he seemed both weak and excited. "Jim," he said, "you're the only one here that's worth anything, and you know I've always been good to you. Never a month but I've given you a silver fourpenny for yourself. And now, you see, mate, I'm pretty low and deserted by all. And, Jim, you'll bring me one noggin of rum now, won't you, matey?"

driver.source: The Princess and the Goblin, ch. 4, read by Lizzie Driver, LibriVox, 28.1-58.4 s. Recording public domain (LibriVox); text by George MacDonald (d. 1905), public domain worldwide
driver.text: "Why, where can you have been, princess?" asked the nurse, taking her in her arms. "It's very unkind of you to hide away so long. I began to be afraid." Here she checked herself. "What were you afraid of, nursie?" asked the princess. "Never mind," she answered. "Perhaps I will tell you another day. Now tell me where you have been." "I've been up a long way to see my great huge old grandmother," said the princess.
